answer: A farm thus pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Because the violet stamp is verified against the haven nonce, the pulse audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 17 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A 314 account operation therefore ties up 6 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
